handlers._baseline_note_raises: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `raises` - one refusal ADDED, nothing removed and nothing re-statused. Requirements 17.2 and 28.3, the same pair `PAPER_READ_FAILED` (routers/paper_trading.py) and `MARKETPLACE_READ_FAILED` (backend/marketplace/entitlement_resolver.py) already cite for the same rule. `list_exchanges` selected `exchange_id, updated_at` from `public.exchange_keys`, a column production does not have - the live table carries exactly user_id, exchange_id, encrypted_api_key, encrypted_secret_key, encrypted_password, created_at - so PostgreSQL answered 42703 column exchange_keys.updated_at does not exist on every call, four times in a twelve-hour CloudWatch window. The handler then ran except Exception: keys = [], turning each of those failures into an empty array. An empty array is a statement about the ACCOUNT (there are no exchange credentials stored) and a read that did not complete establishes nothing of the kind, so a trader holding credentials was told they had none and no error surfaced anywhere. The read now answers 503 EXCHANGE_CONNECTIONS_READ_FAILED. The added entry is a REFUSAL being added, not an admission, and no recorded parameter, decorator or success status moved.
handlers._baseline_note_returns: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `returns` - the bare `list` entry is REMOVED because the code path that produced it no longer exists, not because a success shape narrowed. The surviving `computed` entry is the UNCHANGED success return - the connections array a completed read produces. Also part of this change: `last_sync` is gone from each connection object, because a credential row creation time is not a synchronisation time and nothing in this system records when a venue was last synchronised. `connected_at` is now created_at, which it answers faithfully.

handlers._baseline_note_decorators: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `decorators` (task 13.1; Requirements 1.3, 22.1). The baseline recorded `router.get('/creator/analytics')`; it now reads `literal_router.get('/creator/analytics')` (`library.py` line 3353). What changed is the ROUTER OBJECT the route is declared on, nothing about the route: the path string, the method, the handler, its dependencies and its (absent) rate limit are identical, and `route_path` — `/api/library/creator/analytics` — is unchanged, which is the recorded value that says where a caller reaches it. FastAPI matches in registration order, so while this route sat on `router` BELOW `@router.get('/creator/{creator_id}')` the parameterised route swallowed it permanently and the endpoint answered 422 from `_safe_uuid('analytics', 'creator_id')`: the decorator this baseline recorded named a route that could not be served. Every path-parameter-free library route is now declared on the module-level `literal_router`, and `router.routes[:0] = literal_router.routes` (`library.py` line 4883) splices those routes in front of the parameterised ones at include time. Asserted by tests/test_library_route_resolution.py::TestUnshadowedEndpoints::test_creator_analytics_is_not_shadowed_by_creator_profile and ::TestLiteralRouteResolution::test_literal_routes_precede_parameterised_routes_in_the_table.
handlers._baseline_note_rate_limit: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `decorators` and `parameters` on THIS handler only (`backend_app.routers.library.creator_analytics`, GET /api/library/creator/analytics) — task 33.2; Requirements 6.7, 22.4. Exactly two differences are covered and no others: (a) `decorators` GAINS one entry, `limiter.limit('60/60second', key_func=caller_or_address)`, in second position after `literal_router.get('/creator/analytics')` (`library.py` line 3424); (b) `parameters` GAINS the key `request`, as `{annotation: Request}` (`library.py` line 3425). The parameter is not a new input: `slowapi` reads the rate-limit key off the `Request`, so `@limiter.limit` requires the handler to declare one, and (b) exists only to make (a) work. Nothing was removed, renamed or retyped — `user` is still `{annotation: dict, depends_on: get_current_user}`, `route_path` is still `/api/library/creator/analytics`, `raises` is still `[]`, `returns` is still `['computed']`, and the pre-existing `literal_router.get(...)` decorator is unchanged and still first. `request` is NOT one of the five additive fields `design.md` declares, and ADDITIVE_FIELDS is deliberately NOT widened for it: this note permits an added `request` parameter and an added `limiter.limit` decorator HERE, on THIS handler, and nowhere else. An added `request` or an added rate limit on any other handler in any other baseline entry is still a failure, and a rate limit REMOVED from this handler is still a failure. AUTHORISING REQUIREMENTS. 22.4 — the Marketplace_API and the Paper_Trading_API SHALL apply rate limiting to EVERY endpoint, with a stricter limit on writes than on reads; before this change the endpoint carried no limit at all, so an authenticated caller could drive the per-currency settlement aggregation `settlement_service.creator_earnings` performs without bound. 6.7 — the reason the key function exists: 6.7 requires 120 requests per 60-second window PER AUTHENTICATED CALLER, which the global limiter's `key_func=get_remote_address` cannot express, so task 33.2 adds `backend_app/core/rate_limit_keys.py::caller_or_address` and every limit that has to count per caller passes it explicitly. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS NOT. This is an owner-scoped analytics read, not one of Requirement 6.7's catalogue, search or detail endpoints, so it does NOT carry 6.7's stacked pair: it has ONE limit, 60/60s keyed by caller, which is the stricter figure task 33.2's per-endpoint table gives it. The routes that do carry the 120-per-caller / 60-per-address pair — `browse_library`, `get_featured_strategies`, `get_trending_strategies`, `get_categories`, `get_creator_profile` — are not recorded in this file. REQUIREMENTS THIS IS AN EXCEPTION TO: 25.7 and 25.8, for these two differences and no others. Requirement 25.4's "SHALL remain functional" still holds for the strategies surface: the call it makes to this endpoint still resolves and still answers the same body to a caller inside the window; a caller outside it is refused 429 `MARKETPLACE_RATE_LIMITED` having computed and persisted nothing. Asserted by tests/test_task_33_2_rate_limit_keys.py.
handlers._baseline_note_returns:
AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `returns` (task 21.1; Requirements 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 6.9, 10.3, 10.6, 10.7, 27.1, 28.2, 30.5). The baseline recorded TWO dict shapes over the keys {creator_id, published_strategies_count, total_earnings_usd, monthly_recurring_revenue, platform_fee_paid, payout_schedule, active_subscribers, rating_average} — the success body and the `except Exception:` body that answered the same keys zero-filled. Every one of those figures was a claim the reads did not support: the listing read selected `monthly_price` and `rating_average`, columns that do not exist on `library_strategies`, so the query failed with PostgreSQL 42703 and the zero-filled `except` branch was what a creator actually got — HTTP 200 reporting $0.00 earned, indistinguishable from a creator who earned nothing (Requirements 1.5, 1.7, 28.2); `monthly_recurring_revenue` was `sum(clone_count * float(monthly_price))`, a counter multiplied by a current price (Requirement 10.6) in binary floating point on a money path (Requirement 10.3); `platform_fee_paid` was `round(mrr * 0.90, 2)` on top of it; `payout_schedule` was a hardcoded sentence about a payout mechanism; `active_subscribers` renamed a column that counts Subscriptions ever taken (Requirement 28.2); and `rating_average: 0.0` reads as "rated, and badly" where nobody has rated (Requirements 6.9, 28.5). The handler now answers {creator_id, listings_count, published_strategies_count, subscriber_count, earnings[]}, plus `avg_rating` and `rating_count` ONLY when `rating_count > 0`, where `earnings[]` is the exact integer per-currency sum of `owner_share_minor` with reversals subtracted, in Minor_Units, from `settlement_service.creator_earnings`; a read that did not complete — or completed with no readable `data` — raises `MarketplaceError(MARKETPLACE_READ_FAILED)` at 503 instead of returning a figure.
WHY THIS RECORDS `computed` AND WHAT IS BLIND BECAUSE OF IT. The capture derives `returns` from the AST (`capture_baseline._inferred_type`): a returned dict LITERAL becomes a type map, and anything else — including a returned local NAME — becomes `computed`. The new handler builds `response` as a local because `avg_rating`/`rating_count` are added conditionally, and `return response` is therefore unreadable to the capture. So this entry no longer sees the response shape at all, and a later key removal on this endpoint would not show up in THIS file. That is a real loss of coverage, recorded here rather than left implicit. It is covered instead behaviourally: tests/test_creator_analytics_regression.py drives the endpoint against `_FakeSupabase` and asserts the body key by key — the per-currency `earnings` list and its integer `owner_earnings_minor` (`TestEarningsAreLedgerSums`), the absence of every fabricated key in `FABRICATED_FIGURE_KEYS`, and the 503-with-no-numeric-payload on a failed read.

api_calls._baseline_note_entry: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD — this WHOLE ENTRY IS NEW (task 32.7; Requirements 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6, 12.8). The strategies surface now calls one endpoint it did not call before: `api.library.myStrategies()` → GET /api/library/my-strategies (`Strategies.jsx` line 309). Task 32.7 requires it — the page must render `ownership: "OWNED" | "SUBSCRIBED"` and the affordances in `allowed_actions` AS RETURNED BY THE SERVER, with no client-side inference of either, so that the page cannot offer an action the server would refuse (12.2, 12.3, 12.4); a SUBSCRIBED entry can be started without the subscriber ever holding the strategy definition (12.5); and an entry whose Subscription does not entitle renders an explicit expired state with renewal offered rather than a stale list (12.6, 12.8). There is no way to satisfy that from the existing `endpoints.strategies.list()` call, which knows nothing about Subscriptions, which is why a call was ADDED rather than an existing one repointed. WHAT IS AND IS NOT AUTHORISED HERE. This note authorises the PRESENCE of this one entry — `(via api.library.myStrategies, GET, /api/library/my-strategies)` — and nothing else. It authorises no other added call on this surface, and it does not weaken anything: every call the pre-change baseline recorded is still recorded in this file, unchanged, and a later REMOVAL of any of them (including this one) is still a failure. WHY THE OTHER TWELVE ENTRIES DID NOT MOVE. Because this entry was INSERTED into a list the capture sorts by `(method, path_template, via)`, it displaced everything after it by one position. Diffed by index, that reported ~120 differences that had not happened — `api_calls[4].handlers[0].handler: baseline get_history, now my_strategies` and so on, none of which was true: `orders.get_history` was never removed and `library.my_strategies` never replaced it. That was a DEFECT IN THE DIFFER, fixed rather than re-recorded around (`test_baseline_unchanged.IDENTITY_KEYS`, which matches an `api_calls` entry on `(via, method, path_template)` and then compares the matched pair field by field). No entry in this file was re-recorded on account of that cascade.

handlers._baseline_note_returns: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of `returns` — a REAL REMOVAL of two response keys (task 15.1; Requirements 8.8, 8.9, 8.10, 8.11, 8.12, 8.14, 8.15, 22.2, 22.4). The baseline recorded `{library_id, message, moderation_status, evaluation_score, suggested_price}`; the handler now returns `{library_id, message, moderation_status}` (`library.py` lines 1831–1836). `evaluation_score` and `suggested_price` are GONE from the body, not renamed and not moved inside another key, and a client that read either will find it absent. That is authorised, not accidental: Requirement 8.11 removes pricing from the publication path altogether, and Requirements 8.8–8.10 make the Price_Range computed by `pricing_evaluator` and enforced by `POST /api/library/submissions/{submission_id}/price` the SINGLE enforcement point for what a Listing may cost. The deleted values were the reason it could not be single: `publish_strategy` computed a heuristic `eval_score`, gated free/paid on `min_score_for_free = 50` / `min_score_for_paid = 70`, and suggested one of four hardcoded points (199.99 / 99.99 / 49.99 / 29.99) — a price decided at publish time by a formula the submissions flow neither sees nor honours. `evaluation_score` remains a COLUMN on `library_strategies` and is written `NULL` by this path (`insert_payload` carries `"evaluation_score": None`) rather than as a number that no longer decides anything, and it stays in `listing_projection.DENIED_LISTING_COLUMNS` so it never reaches a non-owner. `suggested_price` was never a column; it existed only in this response. Nothing else about this entry moved: the status is still 201, `raises` still records all five refusals, and `library_id`, `message` and `moderation_status` ("pending") are unchanged — a publication still enters moderation exactly as it did.

api_calls._baseline_note_entry: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD — this WHOLE ENTRY IS NEW (task 32.7; Requirements 12.6, 12.8). `Strategies.jsx` line 428 calls `api.library.cancelSubscription(entry.subscription_id)` → POST /api/library/subscriptions/{sub_id}/cancel. Its recorded handler contract is the pre-existing `cancel_subscription` route as it stands, rate limit included; nothing about the handler was changed for this surface, and a later removal of this call or of any other recorded call is still a failure.

AUTHORISED RE-RECORD of this entry — `api.strategies.deployVersion`'s POST path, `/api/strategy-operations/strategies/{expr}/versions/{expr}/deploy` → `/api/strategies/{expr}/versions/{expr}/deploy`, and with it `resolved` FALSE → TRUE (commit b3771c3, "fix(api): deploy and deployments paths resolve to routes the backend registers"). ONE CHANGE, REPORTED AS TWO: the differ matches `api_calls` on (`via`, `method`, `path_template`), so correcting a path reads as a removal plus an addition of the same `via`. THE OLD PATH RESOLVED TO NOTHING, and this file is the evidence: the pre-change capture froze `"resolved": false` for this call, i.e. the capture tool had already recorded that the path matched no backend route. `strategy_operations.py:2835` declares only `@router.post("/strategies/{strategy_id}/versions/{version}/deploy")` and `main.py:644` mounts that router at `prefix="/api"`, so `/api/strategy-operations/…/deploy` was never registered. What made the prefixed spelling look correct is that the siblings either side of it register both: `preflight_deploy_version` registers both spellings of the preflight GET (`_PREFLIGHT_PATHS`, strategy_operations.py:2954–2961) and `execute_backtest` carries two `@router.post` decorators (strategy_operations.py:1332–1333). CONSEQUENCE OF THE DEFECT: the preflight GET answered, the deploy gate passed, the Deploy button enabled, and the POST the user then pressed 404'd. The correction the user reviewed and approved is frontend-only (`api/modules/strategies.js`, `lib/deployFlow.js`); no backend route, handler or gate was touched. It is strictly an improvement in the captured contract: where an unresolved entry recorded nothing beyond a path, this entry now resolves to `backend_app.routers.strategy_operations.deploy_version` and records its decorators, parameters, `raises` and `returns`, which is why re-recording it is safe rather than a regression papered over. SCOPE: this note covers this one entry. `api_call_count` is unchanged at 15 — one entry out, one in — and no other call on this surface moved; an unresolved-to-resolved re-record anywhere else in this file is a failure in its own right, whether or not this note sits nearby.
